threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of 'the underground'—a dead giveaway you're fresh off the bus from the suburbs.
Caught the 35 from Brixton last night; a bloke serenading everyone with a ukelele. Made the usual graffiti-covered seats feel like an open mic night.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was really living here when I saw a guy juggling flaming torches outside the bakery at 8 AM, while the queue for pastries just kept getting longer.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find a late-night kebab stand doubling as an art gallery, where the chef is actually an aspiring painter. Wild.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they’ve figured out how to dodge the Muni delays by timing their coffee runs perfectly around the Civic Center chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading the bus line at Civic Center today. Muni went full stop for his show. Can’t tell if he was their best distraction or just part of the chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia's just about Gaudí, but they miss out on the tiny, unmarked cafés where real locals gather for their morning café amb llet.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll see them staring at the metro map like it’s a treasure map, usually in the wrong direction, and often ask to find ‘Plaza Catalunya’.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of 'the Overground.' Welcome to the real Hackney, where the tracks are just as important as the brunch spots.
Saw a guy serenading the driver on the 59 last night—ended with a bow when we hit Stockwell. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Last weekend, I sat on the steps of a canal and listened to a spontaneous jam session. That's when it hit me—this place vibrates with creativity.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice the spontaneous open-air parties at Boxhagener Platz? Totally unique vibe; you'll find a mix of techno and old-school folk tunes.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their instinct to sidestep dog owners at Civic Center. Tourists just stand there, oblivious, while we're all on high alert.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Spotted a guy in a full tuxedo waiting for the 21, chatting up a pigeon as if it were his date. Only in SF, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the parks, but it's really the late-night xurros at the corner shop that hold the neighborhood's secrets.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones staring at the metro map like it’s a treasure map, utterly lost yet determined to find the way to Sagrada Família.
